content:
anita (support): bumping this thread — customer acme_sre opened an escalation: intermittent "Invalid JSON" errors from JSON mode when streaming multipart responses. They see it only after ~3-5 requests on the same client process.

anita (support): paste from customer logs:
```
LibError: Unexpected token } in JSON at position 204
  at parse (/usr/local/lib/node_modules/app/node_modules/parse-json/index.js:52:15)
  at IncomingMessage.<anonymous> (stream-reader.js:88:27)
  at IncomingMessage.emit (events.js:327:22)
  at endReadableNT (_stream_readable.js:1220:12)
```

anita (support): customer says toggling keep-alive to false makes the error go away. They provided a raw capture of the response chunks — looks like we interleave multipart boundaries with JSON fragments: 
```
--BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

{"event":"delta","payload":{"choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hel""
--BOUNDARY
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8

"lo"}}]}}
--BOUNDARY--
```

anita (support): notice the second part starts with a string fragment "lo" which, when appended to the previous chunk incorrectly, produces a malformed document. Customer is using our TS SDK v0.19.0 with keepAlive agent pooled across requests and the same socket reused.

jordan (devx): can you confirm SDK versions for all clients? this smells like a streaming parser instance being reused across multipart parts.

anita (support): confirmed: TS 0.19.0, Python 0.23.1, Go 0.15.2. Customer repros on TS and Py.

samir (eng-runtime): assigned, thanks. quick hypothesis: our JSON-mode streaming parser keeps partial buffer state and we don't fully reset it on part boundary when using multipart/chunked responses. connection reuse (keep-alive) amplifies it. can you share trace id and example curl that reproduces?

acme_sre: trace=trace-7f3a9b22, repro cURL (sanitized):
```
curl -v -H "Accept: multipart/mixed; boundary=BOUNDARY" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/jsonmode -N
```

acme_sre: the reproduction is deterministic when we reuse the same long-lived agent/pool (node http.Agent keepAlive: true). If we set `Connection: close` it stops failing.

marie (eng-ml): workaround: on server side we should ensure each multipart part is a self-contained JSON document (never start a string in one part and finish it in the next). But we should fix parser behavior too — treat each boundary as a hard reset. Possible quick patch: parser.resetOnBoundary = true; later we can make it configurable.

jordan (devx): +1 on reset. also add strict validation when concatenating chunks so a leading `"` at beginning of part can't be treated as continuation of previous buffer.

samir (eng-runtime): creating a small repro harness now to simulate pooled sockets and chunk fragmentation. plan: 1) reproduce locally with node http server that emits fragments as above 2) run SDKs against it 3) run bisect to find commit where parser behavior changed.

anita (support): added logs from customer showing exact chunk sizes and timings (uploaded to ticket): https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-4821 (internal link).

deploy-bot: I just pushed a dev build with parser.resetOnBoundary flag set to true on runtime-dev. Node/Py SDKs still need a fix; runtime change prevents the malformed concat today.

acme_sre: confirmed patch on runtime-dev stops the error for now. thanks. Will you backport to prod?

samir (eng-runtime): yes — will schedule prod rollout after we add unit tests. Quick followups: can SDKs defensively reset parser state on response boundary too? that would cover old runtimes.

jordan (devx): I'll prototype a small change in TS and Py SDKs to reinitialize the streaming parser whenever a multipart boundary token is seen. keeps perf impact minimal.

marie (eng-ml): tests to add: fuzzed chunk boundaries, partial unicode escape across parts, and repeated reuse of same parser instance across 1000 short requests.

anita (support): customer is happy with the dev fix for now; will mark CS ticket pending prod rollout. I'll follow up once prod deploy is scheduled. :raised_hands:

samir (eng-runtime): logging action items: (1) prod rollout of runtime boundary-reset patch, (2) TS/Py SDK defensive reset change + release, (3) add unit/integration tests (fuzz chunking), (4) docs note about multipart + JSON-mode gotchas.

acme_sre: thank you all for fast triage. they blocked us from launching a rollout earlier today. we can continue with our work after prod patch.

anita (support): closing loop for now — will reopen thread once prod is live or SDK releases are out.
